n01-open

Agents are only as good as the context they get. <break time='200ms'/> Microsoft IQ gives them three kinds: <break time='120ms'/> Work IQ for how people work, <break time='120ms'/> Fabric IQ for what the business data means, <break time='120ms'/> and Foundry IQ for the knowledge an agent retrieves.
n02-title
Here's how to design with them in the Azure Architecture Diagram Builder.
n03-brief
A commercial insurer wants an underwriting copilot in Microsoft Teams. <break time='150ms'/> The brief names the IQ services the way the customer would.
n04-gen
Generate. <break time='120ms'/> AADB knows these services, so each one stays its own node with its own icon, instead of being folded into Fabric or AI Search.
n05-workiq
Work IQ brings in the broker emails and meetings from Microsoft 365. <break time='120ms'/> It's licensed with Microsoft 365 Copilot, so it's shown as external, and adds nothing to the Azure bill.
n06-foundryiq
Foundry IQ is the agent's knowledge base over the underwriting guidelines. <break time='120ms'/> It runs on Azure AI Search, and that's how it's priced.
n07-fabriciq
Fabric IQ is the business ontology over OneLake: <break time='100ms'/> policies, claims and brokers, and how they relate.
n08-opsagent
And a Fabric Operations Agent watches submissions as they arrive, and flags the risky ones.
n09-capacity
Fabric items don't bill on their own. They run on a Fabric capacity. <break time='150ms'/> AADB always includes the capacity, even when the model forgets it, so the run rate is right.
n10-ask
Now the underwriters want to trace how brokers, policies and claims are connected. <break time='120ms'/> Ask Guided Chat for a Graph Model.
n11-wait
The change is reviewed before it lands.
n12-added
The Graph Model joins the design, built over the Fabric IQ ontology, as asked.
n13-same-cost
It runs on the same capacity, so the monthly cost doesn't change.
n13-new-cost
The run rate updates with the change.
n14-close
Work IQ, Fabric IQ and Foundry IQ on one diagram, <break time='120ms'/> each where it belongs, and priced the way it's billed. <break time='150ms'/> Ready to validate, deploy and share.
